scope: Inherited U-shaped mountain valleys attached to mapped glacial erosion and existing drainage.
status: Numerical and actual-world tests passed; native screenshots and moving performance pending.

research.application: Glacial troughs widen pre-existing valleys, with broad floors and steep enclosing sides.
Use linked glaciation, bedrock and drainage rather than an arbitrary scenic bowl in every mountain region.

placement: Both ends of an existing upland drainage reach carry mapped glacial erosion.
Require substantial inherited mountain relief and a significant channel; exclude ocean endpoints and low/coastal floors.
Erode inherited ground only. Preserve accepted standing lakes and the river's narrower modern channel/alluvium.
implementation: Static finite U-profile cuts; no new scenery mesh, draw call, texture sample or live glacier tick.
Numeric compressed-row index retains no per-face managed list/reference graph.
Construct before river bank fitting; final reconciled river datums are shared by the trough floor.
Physical rock-wall exposure reaches the existing soil/material/rooted vegetation path.
Local terrain and amplification versions invalidate incompatible derived datums.

cache.limits: Full local terrain preparation observations, not the isolated cost of glacial index construction or total game startup.

limits: Static morphological approximation, not a glacier flow/erosion simulation.
This pass does not add cirques, hanging lakes, overhangs or ocean-connected fjords.
Numerical evidence is not visual acceptance or proof of a universal frame floor.
